h1: The 8 Best Room Dividers on Wheels of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Room Dividers on Wheels: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best room dividers on wheels for 2026, from single panels to 6-panel and soundproof models, with specs and who each suits.
summary: The SUNALLY 4-panel divider is the best room divider on wheels, combining widened feet, lockable silent casters and thick 240gsm fabric. The HOMSCREENER four-panel with double hinges suits awkward corners, and the GOFLAME folds compact for renters. For big open floor plans, the 132 inch HOMSCREENER six-panel gives the widest span.
intro: Most room divider roundups obsess over fabric color and panel count, then ignore the one thing that decides whether the screen is safe to live with: what happens when you lean on it or bump it with a laundry basket. A tall frame on a skinny base and wheels that will not lock is a rolling accident waiting for a quiet evening.

We ranked eight wheeled dividers from their listing specs: overall size, panel count, caster count and lock design, base length, fabric weight and price bucket. We rated stability features ahead of finish or style, since a divider that wanders is unusable. All sizes and weights below are the figures the sellers publish.

products.name: SUNALLY 4-Panel Room Divider with Lockable Wheels
products.verdict: The best balance of fabric, stability and price.
products.description:
The SUNALLY is 88 inches wide and 72 inches tall, with four panels of 240gsm polyester over a powder-coated steel frame. Each panel carries four silent PE lockable wheels, and extended widened feet add stability. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It wins because it handles the safety question better than anything near it. Widened feet matter more than panel count, and this is the only one here that markets them. The HOMSCREENER below it has a longer metal base but a less specific wheel story, so the lead comes down to stability engineering rather than fabric.

Buy it for a bedroom or studio where the screen moves occasionally. Skip it if you need a six-panel span. It is also bulky when folded away.
products.skipIf: You need a very wide span.

products.name: HOMSCREENER 4-Panel Room Divider on Wheels
products.verdict: Double hinges that bend around irregular layouts.
products.description:
HOMSCREENER's four-panel model is 88 inches wide and 71.3 inches tall, using 240gsm polyester and steel. It has ten self-locking universal PE castors, a 17.7 inch metal base, the longest in the four-panel group, and double hinges that allow L, W, C and Z shapes.

It ranks second only because the SUNALLY's wheel arrangement is described in more detail. In pure geometry this one is arguably the more flexible screen, since the double hinge lets it wrap around a nook or couch without gaps. The long base helps resist tipping when you use those bent shapes.

Buy it for irregular rooms, corner offices or open-plan spaces that need odd angles. Skip it if you want a flat wall, and expect it to be heavy to push around.

products.name: GOFLAME 4-Panel Rolling Room Divider
products.verdict: Folds compact and bends into L, W or C shapes.
products.description:
GOFLAME's divider measures 89 inches wide by 68 inches tall and uses polyester over metal. It carries ten lockable 360 degree swivel wheels with individual brakes, shapes into L, W or C layouts and folds down to 22 inches wide. Price sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Third place reflects its modest height and lighter fabric. At 68 inches it is shorter than the SUNALLY and the HOMSCREENER, which matters for privacy if you are tall. In return you get individual brakes on each wheel and the best storage story of the group, which is hard to beat when the screen leaves the room every few weeks.

Buy it if you rent and store the divider often. Skip it if sightlines at standing height are the point.

products.name: HOMSCREENER 6-Panel Room Divider on Wheels
products.verdict: A 132 inch wide divider for open floor plans.
products.description:
HOMSCREENER's six-panel unit is 132 inches wide and 72 tall, built with 240gsm polyester on a scratch-resistant, rust-proof steel tube frame. It has eight self-lockable PE wheels and, per the listing, the thickest fabric among the six-panel picks. The ticket is $100 to $200.

Fourth place follows from the wheel math: eight wheels spread over six panels give fewer locks per panel than the four-panel models give. Width is its real advantage: 132 inches will split a loft or a living room in a way no 88 inch screen can. The price step up is the cost of that span.

Buy it for large, open rooms. Skip it if your space is small, because it is hard to store and overkill for a single corner.

products.name: Giantex 6-Panel Room Divider with Lockable Casters
products.verdict: Fourteen lockable casters, the most in this ranking.
products.description:
Giantex sells a six-panel divider at 132 by 68 inches, covered in polyester over a powder-coated metal frame with durable buckle connections. It lists 14 lockable universal casters, the most in this ranking, though each wheel is only 1.5 inches across. Price bucket is $100 to $200.

It ranks fifth because tiny wheels can struggle on thick carpet, even with many of them, and the 68 inch height gives less privacy than the 72 inch leaders. The huge caster count does give excellent parking stability on a hard floor, which is what many buyers care about most.

Buy it for hardwood or tile and a wide span. Skip it if your floor is plush carpet, where the small wheels will drag.

products.name: Kokorona 6-Panel Room Divider with Lockable Wheels
products.verdict: Gap-cover strips remove sightlines at the hinges.
products.description:
Kokorona builds a six-panel screen 119 inches wide and 70 inches tall from 180gsm polyester over iron. It has seven sets of lockable wheels, large support feet and gap-cover strips to close hinge sightlines, with fabric listed as waterproof and tear-resistant. Price bucket is $100 to $200.

It sits sixth because the fabric is lighter than the 240gsm used on the models above, and the price is higher than the four-panel leaders. The gap strips are its standout idea, since hinge gaps are where people peek through folding screens.

Buy it when full visual privacy matters most, such as a shared bedroom or a work corner. Skip it if you want thick, opaque fabric, where the 240gsm models are stronger.

products.name: HOMSCREENER 3-Panel Soundproof Room Divider on Wheels
products.verdict: A tackable, noise-absorbing panel for home offices.
products.description:
HOMSCREENER's soundproof divider has three panels, measures 72 inches wide by 66 tall and uses ECO PET plus polyester fabric. The listing cites 85 percent or more noise absorption, a tackable surface, zipper connections and 12 self-locking wheels. It is the priciest here, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks seventh because it spans only 72 inches and costs the most. The value is specialized: absorbing sound and letting you pin papers to the surface suit a home office far better than any fabric screen above it.

Buy it for a work-from-home setup or a recording corner where noise matters. Skip it if you need a wide divider, since the narrow span cannot close off a large opening and ordinary fabric screens do not absorb sound.

products.name: MAYOLIAH Single Large Panel Rolling Room Divider
products.verdict: The cheapest option, a single non-see-through panel.
products.description:
MAYOLIAH sells a single large panel of 71 by 75 inches in waterproof, non-see-through fabric over iron. It has four lockable wheels, a no-gap design with six fasteners and costs in the $25 to $50 bucket, the lowest here.

It lands last because a single panel cannot bend, fold into shapes or wrap a corner. There is nothing wrong with the idea, but flexibility is what most buyers want from a divider, and every multi-panel option above delivers it. What you get instead is simple, gap-free coverage for little money.

Buy it for one fixed spot, such as hiding a desk or a laundry area. Skip it if your layout changes or you need a long span.

methodology.title: Stability
methodology.description: Base width, foot design and caster count.

whatMatters.detail: Wheel locks hold the divider in place once it is positioned. Without them, a screen drifts when bumped or when a door opens. The best designs give each wheel its own brake. Check the listing for self-locking or individually braked wheels. GOFLAME lists individual brakes, and the SUNALLY lists lockable silent wheels.

Base width is the foot length that resists tipping. A tall screen on narrow feet can fall forward when leaned on, so wide bases are a safety feature. Look for foot dimensions in the specs. The HOMSCREENER four-panel lists a 17.7 inch base, and the SUNALLY highlights widened feet.

Fabric weight, quoted in gsm, shows how thick the cloth is. Heavier fabric hides silhouettes and lasts longer, so 240gsm blocks sight better than 180gsm. Find the gsm number in the listing. The SUNALLY and both HOMSCREENER dividers use 240gsm, while Kokorona uses 180gsm.

Panel count sets how much floor the screen can span and how many shapes it can make. More panels cover more space but are harder to store and push. Measure your gap before buying. Four panels span about 88 inches here, while six reach 119 to 132 inches.

Floor type decides whether small casters roll or stick. Hard floors let small wheels glide, while thick carpet can stop them. Note your flooring before ordering and compare wheel size where the listing gives it. Giantex lists 1.5 inch wheels, which suit hard floors better than carpet.

faq.a: Standard fabric screens block sight, not sound. Of the eight, only the HOMSCREENER three-panel soundproof divider lists a figure, with 85 percent or more noise absorption. For an office or recording corner, it is the one to buy.

Hard PE wheels can mark soft flooring such as vinyl or finished wood if dirt gets trapped under them. Check the wheel material, wipe the floor before moving a loaded screen, and keep the locks on when parked, as on the SUNALLY.

Multi-panel units fold, with the GOFLAME shrinking to 22 inches wide. The MAYOLIAH is a single panel and does not fold, which makes it simpler to use but awkward to store. Check how much closet depth you actually have first.

Wide bases help a lot. The HOMSCREENER four-panel has a 17.7 inch metal base and the SUNALLY has widened feet. Even so, lock the wheels whenever the screen is parked and avoid leaning on the top edge.

faq.q: How do I clean the fabric?
faq.a: Wipe the fabric with a damp cloth and mild soap. Waterproof options such as the Kokorona and MAYOLIAH clean up easily. Dry it before folding the screen away, and vacuum the hinges and wheels occasionally to prevent grit.

Only with larger wheels. Giantex lists 1.5 inch casters, which can struggle on thick pile even with 14 of them. On low-pile carpet the HOMSCREENER or SUNALLY roll better, and lifting rather than pushing helps on any rug.

finalTake: The SUNALLY 4-panel is the room divider on wheels most people should buy, because its widened feet, lockable wheels and 240gsm fabric solve stability and privacy together. Pick the HOMSCREENER four-panel for awkward corners, the GOFLAME if you store it often and the six-panel HOMSCREENER for open floor plans. Always lock the wheels, whichever you choose.
